# Anthropic stock sinks below IPO price. What history says happens next.

 Story by Callum Keown 

The stock market’s shiny new toy has already been discarded.

Anthropic stock fell 7.4% to $81.12 in early trading Tuesday, dropping below its IPO price of $83. The shares are on track for a third consecutive fall after their first-day bump.

It’s a rapid decline but it isn’t that unusual for megacap companies—and isn’t necessarily a bad omen. Meta Platforms, or Facebook at the time, fell below its initial public offering price after one trading day, while Amazon and Tesla achieved the feat after four days, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Meta is up 1,656% since, Amazon has climbed 357,819%, and Tesla has risen 35,790%, based on price returns. Though, their valuations were nowhere near Anthropic’s $1 trillion-plus market cap.

The most recent example is SpaceX, which dropped under its $135 June IPO price after 22 trading days. The stock was still under that level Tuesday, trading at around $129.

At the other end of the scale, it took Google 4,585 trading days and Microsoft 5,715.

Anthropic, a frontier artificial-intelligence lab, missed out on the Nvidia-fueled rally Monday—falling 1.4% as other AI-exposed stocks booked gains of up to 20% on the stock market’s best day since April 2025.

It’s likely investors were buying the dip in beaten-down names instead—most notably Nvidia, which surged 32% following the dramatic return of Jensen Huang as CEO.

Now, the stock is being dragged lower along with the broader AI ecosystem.

The hype around the company’s IPO has evaporated quickly. The timing hasn’t been great, coning in the middle of the sharp AI selloff. It rose 17% on its trading debut Thursday as the broader stock market took a tumble. But then fell 8.5% on Friday.

After a few days of trading out of kilter with the broader AI trade, it’s moving lower with everything else Tuesday.

The problem for Anthropic now is it’s the stock market’s first and only pure-play AI developer. In the good times that’s brilliant, in the bad times it’s far more exposed.
